v.q: You must check quickly whether a transaction id has already been processed, and order does not matter. Which collection fits best?
v.w: A set answers membership questions. `ArrayList.contains` is O(n), so a loop over many ids becomes O(n²).

v.q: Which collection suits a lookup of an id in a set of 10 million ids?
v.w: HashSet.contains is O(1) on average. The list classes scan every element.

v.q: What happens when `ArrayList` is full and you call `add`?
o: It allocates a larger array (about 1.5×) and copies the elements
It throws an `IllegalStateException` for a full list
It links a new node to the end of the list
It overwrites the oldest element in the array
v.w: The copy is O(n) but rare, so appending is amortised O(1). Pre-size with `new ArrayList<>(n)` when you know the size.

v.q: Which statement about ArrayList is NOT true?
o: Adding to a full list throws an exception
It grows by allocating a larger array
v.w: ArrayList is unbounded and resizes automatically. Fixed-size lists such as Arrays.asList throw on add.

v.q: A for-each loop over a list calls `list.remove(item)` inside the body. What is the usual result?
o: The item is removed and the loop continues normally
The loop restarts from the first element
v.w: The iterator's expected `modCount` no longer matches. Use `removeIf` or `Iterator.remove()` instead.

v.q: Which loop can safely remove items from a list while iterating?
o: A for-each over the list with list.add
A stream calling list.remove inside forEach
v.w: Iterator.remove updates the modification count, so no ConcurrentModificationException is thrown.

v.q: What does `PriorityQueue` guarantee about iteration order?
o: Nothing useful: only `poll` returns elements in priority order
Elements come out sorted from smallest to largest
Elements come out in insertion order
Elements come out in reverse sorted order
v.w: It is a binary heap. The head is the smallest, but the rest of the array is only partially ordered. Poll repeatedly to get sorted output.

v.q: Which method returns the highest-priority element of a PriorityQueue and removes it?
v.w: poll removes the head. peek only looks at it. Iteration order is not priority order.

v.q: Which is the best choice for a stack or a simple FIFO queue in single-threaded code?
v.w: `ArrayDeque` is a circular array with O(1) at both ends and no node overhead. `Stack` and `Vector` are legacy synchronized classes.

v.q: Which class is NOT a good choice for a new stack?
v.w: Stack is a legacy synchronised class built on Vector. ArrayDeque is the usual replacement.

v.q: `Collections.unmodifiableList(list)` is returned from a method. The owner later adds an element to `list`. What does the caller see?
o: The new element, because the wrapper is only a read-only view
The old contents, because the wrapper copied the list
An empty list, because the wrapper was invalidated
v.w: An unmodifiable wrapper blocks changes through itself, not through the original. `List.copyOf` makes an independent immutable snapshot.

v.q: Which method returns an unmodifiable collection that is a copy and does not follow later changes?
v.w: unmodifiableList is a live view. List.copyOf takes an immutable snapshot.

v.q: A `TreeSet<BigDecimal>` receives `new BigDecimal("1.0")` and then `new BigDecimal("1.00")`. How many elements does it hold?
o: One, because `compareTo` treats them as equal
Two, because `equals` treats them as different
Zero, because both values are rejected
Two, because the scale is different
v.w: `TreeSet` uses `compareTo`, which ignores scale. A `HashSet` uses `equals`, which does not, so it would keep both.

v.q: Two keys are equal by compareTo but not by equals. Which collection treats them as one?
v.w: Tree-based collections use compareTo. Hash-based collections use equals and hashCode.

v.q: What is a safe, idiomatic way to remove duplicates from a list while keeping first-seen order?
v.w: `HashSet` loses order and `TreeSet` sorts. `LinkedHashSet` removes duplicates and remembers insertion order. `stream().distinct()` also works.

v.q: Which collection keeps first-seen order and has no duplicates?
v.w: LinkedHashSet adds a linked list to the hash table to remember insertion order.
